meta.research_basis: Independent research: PitchBook and web search; company site and most articles could not be opened
meta.alert: Five-month-old company built inside its lead investor, Eclipse; the CEO is still listed as Eclipse's Chief AI Officer [1,4]. noetive.ai and most articles could not be opened, so product detail rests on PitchBook and launch-coverage excerpts.

company.name: Noetive
company.headquarters: Los Altos, CA [1] (press says San Francisco)
company.one_liner: AI agents plus in-house floor sensors that take over operational decisions such as production planning in plants and logistics; Eclipse-built, one named customer, $41M seed [1,2].

sections.company_product: Agents run on top of a customer's existing systems and take over operational decisions, fed by a multimodal sensing pod Noetive designs: an "intelligence of record" [2] {CR}. Targets: manufacturing, logistics, energy, data centers [2].

technology.text: A core model (the "brain") learns how one operation runs from system data and pod signals; each deployment is meant to improve the shared model [2] {CR}.
bullets: **Not disclosed:** whether the brain is a trained model or agents on frontier LLMs, what the pod senses, how many pods are installed {UNK}.
**Integration:** reads Steuben's system data plus floor conditions [2]; whether agents write plans back to ERP or only advise is not disclosed {UNK}.

**Likely moat, if any:** operating data (plans, outcomes, floor signals) compounding across sites, plus planner reliance; not the model {INF}. Own pods add data rivals lack but slow rollout versus software on existing cameras.

market.text: Wedge: production planning in food and beverage plants, today mostly ERP plus spreadsheets.
bullets: **Palantir AIP:** production scheduling over ERP, MES and PLM data [6]; the default operational layer.
**Kinaxis:** Maestro planning suite adding agents [7]; heavy for mid-size plants.
**Archetype AI:** sensor-data foundation model, $35M Series A Nov 2025 [5]; closest on sensing.

sections.team_financing: CEO Amir Frenkel: about a decade as Meta VP (GenAI, XR), earlier Google and Amazon [1,3]; Eclipse's Chief AI Officer since April 2026, and Noetive formed inside Eclipse [2]. CPO Dan Barak founded Stackbit (sold to Netlify) after Lyft and Meta [3]. Eclipse led, with eight funds and 11 angels (Bosworth, Al-Dahle, Schroepfer) [1]. No founder with plant operations experience disclosed {UNK}.
sections.traction: Sole named customer Steuben Foods (aseptic contract manufacturer): its executive Menachem Katz says planning that ran monthly over a week now runs daily in minutes [2]. Design partnership; paid status, vendor effort unknown {UNK}. PitchBook lists revenue, no figures [1].

perspective.interesting: A customer-quoted week-to-minutes planning gain [2] is a concrete signal at five months. Interesting if it holds without Noetive engineers and transfers to a second plant {INF}.
perspective.validate: Product versus per-site engineering; and Eclipse dependency (it built the company and employs the CEO [1,2]): check terms, board and room for an outside Series A lead.
perspective.fit: Fits the industrial AI focus. Planning and inbound logistics at Volkswagen Group component plants could match once results extend beyond food {INF}. No portfolio overlap found.

questions.question: At Steuben, which systems do you read and write, who signs off the daily plan, and how many of your engineer-days did it take?
What did your second design partner reuse from the Steuben model, and what was rebuilt?
What does the pod capture at Steuben that ERP data missed, and how much gain remains without it?
